extracted.intended_audience: general readers, clinicians, researchers, and potential authors looking for an overview of the Annals of Internal Medicine
extracted.subtask_description: Summarize the Annals of Internal Medicine's scope, content types, publication practices, discoverability, and measures of influence — useful for readers, researchers, and prospective authors who need a high-level picture of the journal's standards and role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope / subject matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Annals publishes content relevant to the field of internal medicine and related sub-specialties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The journal covers material relevant to clinical practice, health care delivery, public health, health care policy, medical education, ethics, and research methodology; content should be relevant to internal medicine clinicians and researchers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of content published
rubrics_metrics.description: Annals publishes a wide variety of original research, review articles, practice guidelines, and commentary relevant to clinical practice, ... In addition, the journal publishes personal narratives that convey the feeling and the art of medicine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepted content includes original research, reviews, practice guidelines, commentary, and personal narratives; selected articles (e.g., patient-oriented content and Clinical Guidelines) may be made freely available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review was introduced by Elkington.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The journal subjects submissions to peer review (historical note confirms the use of peer review as the evaluation process for articles).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication frequency and formats
rubrics_metrics.description: New content is published online weekly and a hard copy is published on the third Tuesday of each month. Frequency: Weekly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors and readers should expect regular weekly online publication and a monthly print issue (third Tuesday).

rubrics_metrics.name: Open access policy / availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Open access: Hybrid. Selected articles in the journal are freely available; these include patient-oriented content and Clinical Guidelines (and related reviews).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The journal operates a hybrid open-access model: some content is freely accessible while other content is subscription/restricted; Clinical Guidelines and certain patient-oriented materials are made openly available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact and citation metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: The most recent (2024) Impact Factor for Annals of Internal Medicine is 15.3 (Clarivate Analytics). According to the new 2024 Journal Citations Reports, Annals remains the most often cited internal medicine journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Impact factor and citation frequency are presented as measures of the journal's influence and prestige; prospective authors may use these metrics to assess the journal's prominence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexing and abstracting / discoverability
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal is abstracted and indexed in: Academic OneFile, Academic Search, BIOSIS Previews, CAB Direct, Chemical Abstracts, CINAHL, Current Contents – Clinical Medicine, Embase, Global Health, Index Medicus/MEDLINE/PubMed, Science Citation Index, Scopus, and others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wide indexing across major bibliographic databases indicates discoverability and accessibility of published work; authors can expect broad indexing for published articles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publisher and editorial leadership
rubrics_metrics.description: Annals of Internal Medicine is published by the American College of Physicians (United States). The current editor-in-chief is Christine Laine, MD, MPH, FACP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The journal's publisher and editor-in-chief signal institutional oversight and editorial direction; authors may infer editorial priorities and governance from the publisher and editorial leadership.
